workflow-bugfix.description: Systematic debugging and fix workflow with end-to-start debugger trace before fix and an explicit-request-only near-end workflow-e2e handoff
workflow-bugfix.intent: Fix a reported defect at the root cause its end-to-start trace proves, guarded by a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it.
workflow-bugfix.name: Bug Fix

outcomeGates.when: A canonical spec or test-case artifact governs the affected area, and behavior or a public contract changed or that spec lacked the case the bug exposed

preActions.injectContext:
BUG FIX (lean, TDD-first). Intent: fix the defect at the root cause its end-to-start trace proves, guarded by a regression test that is RED before the fix and GREEN after.
FIRST: triage size (XS/S/M/L/XL), kind and risk per .claude/skills/workflow-bugfix/SKILL.md; the triage selects which optional steps run. Gate steps always run; core and optional steps follow the /start-workflow Step Execution Protocol, one deviation-log line each.
NON-NEGOTIABLE:
- /debug-investigate owns discovery AND root cause (there is no separate /investigate step). END-TO-START TRACE: start at the observed final state/output, trace backward through reader, storage/projection, writer, consumer/job and producer, enumerate every feeder path, build a hypothesis matrix and weigh environment causes. BLOCKED until the owning fix layer and forward convergence proof are written.
- CODE BUG vs SPEC BUG before any regression TC or test: Code Bug (spec right, code diverged) -> TCs for the intended behavior; Spec Bug (spec documents the wrong behavior) -> /spec [mode=amend] first; Ambiguous -> ask the user. Never encode buggy behavior into specs or tests.
- RED/GREEN: the first /integration-test must FAIL on the bug before /fix; after the fix the regression and affected tests must PASS in this run (/integration-test-verify). Tests name the Business Intent / Invariant Guarded; for lifecycle/state logic assert state before/after and invalid-transition rejection.
- /plan earns its cost for size M+, a Spec Bug, several TCs, cross-module, public-contract/data/security fixes or several candidate fix layers; otherwise /fix plans inline and the investigation report records fix layer, blast radius and rollback.
- When the bug touches a [HARD] rule or invariant, regression TCs add invariant/property cases (mutation-kill bar, not line coverage) and each behavior-changing finding updates BOTH spec and tests.
- Spec sync runs when a canonical spec or TC changed, or specified behavior or a public contract changed (business spec root {SPEC_ROOT}).
- /workflow-review-changes runs INLINE in the main session and converges the review of the whole package (spec + tests + fix); it owns the test-quality review and the docs/domain-entity reference refresh.
- /workflow-e2e --source=context only on an explicit user E2E request; /demo-guide only for user-facing changes.
PERFORMANCE-SDD ROUTE: a performance bug runs /performance-review with SLA/benchmark evidence (target metric, baseline, measurement command, regression budget); keep functional no-regression checks when behavior can change; update specs/docs for a changed SLA or behavior boundary.
CONTEXT: shared/sdd-artifact-contract.md in the active skills root, docs/project-config.json and the docs index. Code-extracted specs are reference-only until accepted.
NEW-UI EXPLORE MOCKUP (conditional, BEFORE plan): only when the fix is large (size M+) and creates new user-facing UI like a feature (a new page/view, component or dialog), run /pbi-mockup --explore --source=<investigation report or amended spec>. MOCKUP SCOPE GATE FIRST (pbi-mockup --explore Step 0, asked at the very START of the mockup step, BEFORE any journey analysis, reading or drafting, so a skip saves tokens and time; a pre-generation confirm, not the post-generation pick): if AskUserQuestion is available ALWAYS ask first: 3, 2 or 1 mockup options, or skip mockups entirely (recommend by scope: new page or multi-view flow -> 3, single component or dialog -> 1-2); skip -> record Mockup: SKIPPED by user and continue without one. If AskUserQuestion is not available, generate ONLY ONE mockup in the recommended direction (best journey fit and best fit with the project design system), auto-select it, record Selection: AUTO-SELECTED — no question tool (1 draft) in direction-approved.md and the plan or run report, and continue. Then Journey Report (UX-1) and design-authority read (UX-2), the chosen 1-3 direction drafts rendered with html-export, each opened in the default browser (node .claude/scripts/open-report.cjs <draft>), then, with 2-3 drafts, AskUserQuestion with one option per draft and your evidence-backed recommendation first labelled (Recommended). Record the user's pick (1 draft -> Selection: USER — 1 option) in tmp/design/<run>/direction-approved.md; the plan's UI Layout builds on the selected mockup. Never pick for the user while they can be asked; if the drafts cannot be shown or AskUserQuestion errors after drafting, AUTO-SELECT the recommended draft (best journey fit + design-system fit) and record Selection: AUTO-SELECTED — <reason> in direction-approved.md and the plan. A fix inside existing UI skips this step with a stated reason. MAIN SESSION ONLY: the mockup scope gate and the pick run in the session that can ask the user, never inside a delegated sub-agent; only the draft builders may be sub-agents.

workflow-e2e.description: Write, update, and verify E2E tests using the configured project runner and a bounded green fix/retest loop; visual evidence follows the request and project contract
workflow-e2e.intent: Author or update E2E coverage for the resolved source scope and converge it to green through the project's configured runner.
workflow-e2e.name: E2E Testing

preActions.injectContext:
E2E WORKFLOW — follow .claude/skills/workflow-e2e/SKILL.md (triage, gates, recommended skills).
FIRST: resolve --source={changes|recording|update-ui|prompt|context|whole} and --visual-review={true|false} from the invocation, request, and project contract (no framework-wide screenshot default; a false value cannot waive a project-required gate), then triage size/kind/risk and record it.
Lifecycle: investigate -> conditional authoring (e2e-test for changes, recording, update-ui; skipped for prompt, context, whole because the loop selects or generates cases) -> e2e-test-verify --fix-loop -> docs-update when tests, baselines, source, or documented behavior changed -> workflow-end -> watzup.
The loop is the single convergence owner: configured run, report-only /experience-review for visual evidence, failure classification, owning-layer fixes, review, fresh bring-up, and same-scope reruns until the configured consecutive green runs pass within the round cap, or escalation.
Invariants: map each selected owner-qualified case (or strict-default TC/section 8 when no native specArtifacts profile applies) to an actual test, assertion, and result; classify SOURCE-WRONG, TEST-WRONG, TEST-NOT-OPTIMAL, ENVIRONMENT-BLOCKED, or AMBIGUOUS before edits; use the runner native waits or an evidenced helper, never a delay as readiness; change no baseline or expectation without explicit acceptance; never weaken, skip, narrow, delete, silence, or auto-accept to obtain green.

preActions.injectContext: LEAN SPEC-SUPPLIED ROUTE: the requested behavior is already written in a canonical spec or TC set, so this route implements it without re-authoring the spec. Read .claude/skills/workflow-implement-spec/SKILL.md. FIRST ACTION: triage size (XS/S/M/L/XL), kind and risk per the SKILL.md Size & Kind Triage; depth follows risk and ambiguity, and the gap review plus every gate hold at every size. ESCALATION (BR-GWF-04): /investigate reads the supplied spec and the affected code, then /spec-clarify runs as a gap review of that spec against the request; when the spec is vague or contradictory, or the requested behavior is not in it, STOP before /plan and ask the user to clarify the spec or switch to workflow-feature, which updates the spec first. Never guess the missing behavior and never drop it silently. SPEC-BASELINE ANCHOR (BR-GWF-05): /plan records the supplied spec as its spec_baseline (plan skill, Supplied-Spec Scope Baseline) and every plan task traces to that baseline; a requirement the baseline lacks goes to "Proposed additions (need approval)" and becomes a question, never a planned task. /spec [mode=sync] runs only when the implemented behavior differs from the supplied spec, and always before /integration-test and the nested /workflow-review-changes (run inline in the main session), so the review sees the synced spec.

applicability.when: The implemented behavior differs from the supplied spec.
applicability.skipReason: The implementation matches the supplied spec, so there is nothing to sync.

preActions.injectContext:
REVIEW CURRENT CHANGES — intent: review the current changes, validate every finding, fix the validated blocking ones at their owning layer, and re-review the fixed state until the round bar clears. The SKILL.md (`.claude/skills/workflow-review-changes/SKILL.md`) owns the procedure; you choose the orchestration.

TRIAGE FIRST: classify the target by size band (XS 1-3 files … XL 300+ files) and change kinds (docs-only, tooling/config, test-only, behavior, public contract, data/schema, security-sensitive, UI, infra/CI, cross-module). The triage selects which optional specialist reviewers run (each occurrence carries its applicability) and how deep; record the review plan in the report before reviewing.

SEVERITY + ROUND-BAR POLICY (MANDATORY):
- Classify each validated finding by shipped consequence, not effort: CRITICAL = immediate material risk (security/authority bypass, secrets or PII exposure, irreversible destructive action, data loss/corruption, silent critical-path failure, or failed binary gate); HIGH = material supported-path correctness, contract, invariant, privacy, authority, compatibility, or likely-harm risk; MEDIUM = bounded consequential edge/resilience/observability/testability/maintainability or local architecture gap; LOW = polish with no credible present correctness, security, privacy, authority, availability, or data-integrity impact.
- Round 1 blocks on every validated severity. Rounds 2-3 block only on validated CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM; LOW-only rounds end immediately and list LOWs as deferred. Never re-tier a finding to obtain a pass. Binary gates (tests, security must-fix, required artifacts, generated parity, policy compliance) block at every round. `NOT VERIFIABLE` is pending evidence, never a LOW escape hatch.

REVIEWERS: `changes-review` runs INLINE in the main session (report-only inside this workflow) in parallel with the whole-target `why-review` sub-agent; advance only after BOTH return. The selected specialists — `architecture-review`, `domain-entities-review`, `performance-review`, `integration-test-review`, `security-review`, `production-readiness-review`, `ui-review` — run with `--report-only` as read-only leaves (no fixes, no user prompts, report under tmp/reports/), dispatched together in one message; advance only after every spawned reviewer returns. `integration-test-review` always runs (coverage map + relevant test results).

FIX PATH (no plan ceremony): consolidate every report into the living changes-review report → `why-review --validate-findings` on findings not already validated by their reviewer → `fix --target=review` on validated blocking findings → `code-simplifier` when code changed → post-fix `why-review` INLINE over the settled whole target → loop within the round budget. Use `/plan` only when the validated fix set is large, cross-module or ambiguous.

MANDATORY GATES:
- SPEC DRIFT ADJUDICATION: every behavior-changing file is adjudicated CODE-WRONG / SPEC-STALE / SPEC-SILENT / AMBIGUOUS (AskUserQuestion) — never normalized because tests are green. Every behavior-changing finding feeds BOTH the spec and the tests (Dual-Feedback Ledger).
- INTEGRATION TEST SYNC: changed business-logic files need a covering test; a gap is surfaced via AskUserQuestion — mandatory, not advisory.
- MULTILINGUAL UI SYNC CHECK: If UI-facing files changed and project localization is multilingual (`localization.enabled` + `supportedLocales.length > 1`), verify translation file updates. If missing, surface via AskUserQuestion — mandatory, not advisory.
- STATE MACHINE DATA ASSERT: lifecycle/state-transition changes need persisted-state assertions and invalid-transition rejection tests.
- DOMAIN-ENTITY REFRESH: `scan --target=domain-entities` runs only when the final diff changes an entity/model, DTO/data contract, persistence schema/migration or entity-sync evidence; otherwise skip it as a pre-action deviation with the cited reason.
- DOC SYNC: review steps flag spec/doc gaps read-only; `docs-update` applies them. Every behavior change ends with its configured canonical owner, profile-declared scenario/case and mapped test assertions in sync.

UNIVERSAL RULES: define success criteria first and loop until observable checks pass; every finding cites file:line evidence and confidence; tests verify the protected intent, not just current behavior.

PROJECT CONTEXT: read docs/project-config.json -> integrationTestVerify (guidance, quickRunCommand, testProjectPattern/testProjects, systemCheckCommand, startupScript) and framework.integrationTestDoc; never hardcode a runner, database, helper or layout.

TRIAGE FIRST (record it): failure load after the first verify (0 = proof-only run; XS 1-3 failures sharing a cause = inline; larger = cluster by signature and module, sweep the environment first, adjudicate cluster by cluster in bounded batches) and the verdict kinds. Optional steps run only when their registry `when` holds; log every other deviation per /start-workflow.
LOOP (owned by /integration-test-verify --fix-loop, INLINE): Goal Contract first; each round runs the default verify pass INLINE over the fixed scope; every failure gets ONE Fault Verdict (SOURCE-WRONG | TEST-WRONG | TEST-NOT-OPTIMAL | ENVIRONMENT-BLOCKED | AMBIGUOUS) from /debug-investigate + report-only /integration-test-review BEFORE any edit; /fix at the owning component (SOURCE-WRONG keeps or strengthens the catching test); every round with a fix runs INLINE report-only /changes-review over the fix diff, validates findings with /why-review --validate-findings and folds them into the same round; Round Integrity Check (executed count never shrinks, skipped never grows, scope never narrows); fresh full re-verify. Round cap 3 -> escalate via AskUserQuestion on no progress across 2 rounds, more failures, lost coverage, an open validated finding, ENVIRONMENT-BLOCKED or AMBIGUOUS. /debug-investigate and /fix are roll-ups of the loop - never a second fix loop after it returns.
